answer: Identity weight comes from stake times time spent clean, not headcount. A key minted an hour ago takes a sliver of the epoch allocation regardless of stake; one that survived many clean epochs compounds. A farm must fund upkeep for thousands of keys through a seasoning period before any carries weight, and each abandoned key resets its clock. Count is a liability: the shallow spread of a dune against one deep island of proven age. An honest operator pays the wait once; a farm pays it per alias, so cost scales with keys, not yield. Seasoning is a glacier that thickens by surviving winters.
